statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-34757 (GHSA-6fr7-g8h7-v645) is a use-after-free when a pointer returned by png_get_PLTE, png_get_tRNS or png_get_hIST is passed back to the matching setter, which frees its buffer before copying from the caller's pointer. Upstream fixed it in libpng 1.6.57 with commit 398cbe3df03f4e11bb031e07f416dfdde3684e8a and the follow-up 55d20aaa322c9274491cda82c5cd4f99b48c6bcc, which applies the same fix to png_set_text, png_set_sPLT and png_set_unknown_chunks. Debian backported both commits to trixie in 1.6.48-1+deb13u5 (DSA-6263-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-34757). The DHI Debian repository publishes one build of the libpng1.6 source, a rebuild of Debian 1.6.48-1+deb13u6, for amd64 and arm64, and it carries both commits: the debug symbols for the shipped libpng16.so.16.48.0 on each architecture (matched by build ID) name the safe_palette, safe_hist and safe_trans buffers and the old_text, old_spalettes and old_unknowns variables that the two commits add to pngset.c. Earlier libpng1.6 builds are no longer published. They sort below this version and read as affected, including the rebuilds of Debian 1.6.48-1+deb13u5, which already carried the fix.
